stem: What is the output of the following code?

options.rationale: `45 < 15` is false, so the first branch is skipped.
Only one branch of an `if-elif-else` runs. (And `45 < 30` is false anyway.)
`45 < 60` is the first true condition, so its block runs and the rest is skipped.
`else` only runs when every condition above it is false, but `45 < 60` is true.

explanation: Python checks the conditions from top to bottom: `45 < 15` is `False`, `45 < 60` is `True`, so it prints `Weeknight recipe` and leaves the structure. The `minutes < 30` branch is unreachable here: anything under 30 is also under 60.

stem: Which branch of this code can never run, whatever value `speed` holds?

options.rationale: Any speed above 80 is also above 50, so the `speed > 50` branch above it always catches it first.
This is the first test, so a speed such as 120 reaches it and runs it.
A speed such as 60 is not above 100 but is above 50, so this branch can run.
Any speed of 50 or less, such as 0, makes every condition false and reaches `else`.

explanation: A branch is unreachable when an earlier condition already covers it. When Python gets to `elif speed > 80`, it already knows `speed > 50` was false, so `speed` is at most 50 and can't be above 80. To fix it, test `speed > 80` before `speed > 50`.

stem: What is the output of the following code?

options.rationale: The last `if` is a separate statement, not part of the chain, so it is checked too.
The `if-elif` stops at `Bronze`, and the separate `if` below starts a new decision that is also true.
In an `if-elif` chain only the first true branch runs, so `Silver` is skipped.
The first chain also runs one branch: `85 >= 50` is true, so `Bronze` is printed.

explanation: In the first structure, `85 >= 50` is the first true condition, so `Bronze` prints and the `elif` is not checked. The second `if` starts a new statement at the left edge, so it is always tested: `85 >= 80` is `True`, and `Gold` prints.

stem: What happens when you run this code?

options.rationale: Python checks the whole structure before running it, and the `elif` after `else` is not allowed.
The code never runs: `elif` can't follow `else`.

options.text: `Not a dog` and then `Meow` are printed
options.rationale: Even in valid code only one branch would run, and here the structure is not valid at all.
`else` must be the last branch, so an `elif` after it is a syntax error.

explanation: `else` closes an `if-elif-else` structure, so it must come last. Putting `elif` after it gives `SyntaxError: 'elif' block follows an 'else' block`, and nothing is printed.

stem: What is the output of the following code?
code:
weather = "fog"
plan = "stay home"
if weather == "sun":
    plan = "beach"
elif weather == "rain":
    plan = "museum"
print("Plan:", plan)

options.rationale: `"fog" == "sun"` is false, so the first branch is skipped.
`"fog" == "rain"` is false too; an `elif` is not a fallback.
Neither condition is true and there is no `else`, so `plan` keeps its first value.
`plan` and `weather` are different variables; the branches never copy `weather` into `plan`.

explanation: Both conditions are `False`. An `if-elif` without `else` can run no branch at all, so neither assignment happens and `plan` is still `"stay home"`.

stem: Which statements about `if-elif-else` are true? (Select TWO)

options.text: The conditions are checked from top to bottom, and only the block of the first true one runs.
options.rationale: Python stops at the first true condition and skips the rest of the structure.

options.text: With an `else` at the end, exactly one branch always runs.
options.rationale: If no condition is true, the `else` block is the fallback.

options.text: If two conditions are true, both of their blocks run.
options.rationale: Only the first true condition counts; later ones are not even checked.

options.text: An `elif` can be placed after the `else`.
options.rationale: `else` must come last; an `elif` after it is a `SyntaxError`.

options.text: Without an `else`, at least one branch always runs.
options.rationale: Without `else`, it is possible that no condition is true and no branch runs.

options.text: `else if` on one line is another way to write `elif`.
options.rationale: Python has no `else if` on one line; the keyword is `elif`.

explanation: In an `if-elif-else`, Python tests the conditions in order and runs only the first true one. The final `else` catches everything left over, so with it exactly one branch runs; without it, possibly none.

stem: Complete the shipping calculator so that it prints `Cost: 3` for a 1 kg parcel.
code:
weight = 1
if weight <= 2:
    cost = 3
__BLANK1__ weight <= 10:
    cost = 6
__BLANK2__:
    cost = 11
print("Cost:", cost)

blanks.rationale: `elif` keeps the second test in the same chain, so it is skipped once the first branch has run. A new `if` would also be true for 1 and change the cost to 6.
The fallback branch has no condition, so it is `else:`. `elif:` and `if:` need a condition.

explanation: `1 <= 2` is `True`, so `cost = 3` runs and the rest of the chain is skipped. With a separate `if` in the middle, `1 <= 10` would also be checked and would overwrite the cost with 6.

stem: A weather app picks a label with `if-elif-elif-elif-else`, one condition per line. Put the conditions in the order they must be tested, from the `if` line down, so that every branch can be reached.
rationale: Each condition is true for every value the ones below it accept, so the strictest one must come first.
explanation: Python runs only the first true branch. If `temp > 0` came first, it would catch 35, 25 and 15 too, and the branches below it would be unreachable. Testing from the highest bar down gives each branch its own range.

stem: Which line, inserted at the marked spot, makes the program print `Good afternoon`?
code:
hour = 14
if hour < 12:
    print("Good morning")
# >>> INSERT <<<
    print("Good afternoon")
else:
    print("Good evening")

options.rationale: `14 < 12` is false, so Python moves on and `14 < 18` is true.
`14 > 18` is false, so the `else` block prints `Good evening`.
`else` never takes a condition, so this is a `SyntaxError`.
This repeats the first test, which already failed, so the branch is redundant and `else` runs.

explanation: The middle branch needs its own condition, so it starts with `elif`. For 14, `hour < 12` is `False` and `hour < 18` is `True`, so `Good afternoon` prints and the `else` is skipped.
